name: Primitive Geometry
text:
# Primitive Geometry


## Overview
Primitive Geometry is the foundational layer of the [Splatting](#23-splatting.md) family that defines how volumetric data is decomposed into explicit geometric or parametric primitives for rasterization [S1, S3, S4, unofficial]. It solves the problem of mapping 3D volumetric information to 2D screen space by treating voxels or data elements as shapes (e.g., spheres, quads, capsules) that are transformed and blended [S1, S3, S4, unofficial]. It differs from [ray-casting](#6080-ray-casting.md) methods by computing contributions per primitive rather than per pixel, and from sibling methods by providing the base definitions for primitive types, projection, and culling that specific implementations like [EWA Splatting](1069-ewa-splatting.md) or [Circle Splat Rendering](2981-circle-splat-rendering.md) refine.

## Shared principles
The splatting family shares the fundamental mechanism of treating volumetric data as a set of geometric or parametric primitives that are transformed and rasterized [S1, S3, S4, unofficial].

1.  **Primitive Representation:** The volume is decomposed into primitives. These may be explicit geometric shapes (cubes, cells, splats) or implicit functions sampled via texture hardware [S1, S3, S4, unofficial]. Each primitive $k$ is defined by its position $\mathbf{p}_k$, density/extinction coefficient $g_k$ or $\rho_k$, and a reconstruction kernel $h$ (typically a Gaussian) [S1, unofficial][S6][S10, unofficial].
2.  **Transformation:** Primitives are transformed from volume space to screen space using the Model-View-Projection (MVP) matrix or specific factorizations (e.g., [shear-warp](#24-shear-warp.md)) [S2, S3, S4, unofficial]. For perspective projections, the kernel shape may be distorted (e.g., [EWA splatting](#1069-ewa-splatting.md)) to account for foreshortening [S6][S10, unofficial].
3.  **Rasterization:** The transformed primitives are projected onto the 2D image plane. This step leverages hardware-accelerated scan-conversion, depth testing, and blending [S1, S2, S3, S4, unofficial]. The contribution of a voxel $D$ to a screen point $(x,y)$ is determined by the [footprint function](#4731-footprint-function-mechanism.md) $F(x,y)$, which is the integral of the 3D kernel along the view direction [S2, unofficial][S6][S10, unofficial]:
    $$ F(x,y) = \int h(x-x_D, y-y_D, z) \, dz $$
    The intensity written to the pixel is modulated by the voxel density:
    $$ P(x,y) = \text{weight}(x,y) \cdot \rho(D) $$
    where $\text{weight}(x,y) = F(x-x_D, y-y_D)$ [S10, unofficial].
4.  **[Compositing](#2436-compositing.md):** Contributions are accumulated to form the final image. This is typically done using [alpha blending](#5750-alpha-blending.md) in back-to-front or front-to-back order to handle transparency correctly [S1, S2, S3, unofficial][S7, book]. Splatting compositing is performed along sheets (all pixels at once for a set of voxels), whereas ray-casting composites along rays (one sample at a time) [S10, unofficial].
5.  **Hardware [Acceleration](#18-acceleration.md):** Most methods in this family rely on GPU rasterization pipelines for performance, enabling real-time interactivity [S1, S2, S3, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Circle Splat Rendering](2981-circle-splat-rendering.md)
Projects volumetric primitives as 2D quads with configurable size and diagonal coverage, enabling efficient frustum culling in clip space. Choose when consistent coverage and explicit quad geometry are required.

### [Line Capsule Primitive](3131-line-capsule-primitive.md)
Replaces exact volumetric line primitives with a computationally cheaper 2D rotationally symmetric profile. Choose for high-density line structures where performance is critical.

### [Tetrahedral Splatting](3181-tetrahedral-splatting.md)
Approximates unstructured tetrahedral meshes with spherical or ellipsoidal splats. Choose for real-time rendering of explicit geometric meshes rather than sampled grids.

### [Voxel Splat Rendering](3730-voxel-splat-rendering.md)
Projects 3D voxels as quads or circles for interactive visualization. Choose for large volumetric datasets requiring real-time slice-based selection and parameter tuning.

### [Decomposition](7254-decomposition.md)
Converts volumetric data into explicit shapes (spheres/slices) based on data mapping. Choose when an object-order approach with explicit discretization is preferred over ray-based methods.

### [Triangle Mesh Splatting](8109-triangle-mesh-splatting.md)
Approximates [splat kernels](#8724-splat-kernels-and-footprints.md) with discrete triangle meshes for hardware rasterization. Choose when trading geometric exactness for significant rendering speed improvements is acceptable.

### [Resonant Brane Splatting](9845-resonant-brane-splatting.md)
Uses 'Branes' with Gaussian-Hermite modes to model local contrast and textures. Choose for arbitrary-scale super-resolution where spatially varying color within a primitive is needed.

## Background
The concept of primitive geometry in volume rendering originates from the shift from ray-based to [object-order rendering](#22-object-order-rendering.md) techniques. Early work by Levoy [S3] and Westover [S4] established the theoretical basis for splatting, treating voxels as 3D kernels projected onto the screen. The family has evolved to include specialized primitives for specific data types, such as lines [S1] and tetrahedra [S1], and has been adapted for modern hardware acceleration [S1, S2, S3]. Recent developments include [Resonant Brane Splatting](#9845-resonant-brane-splatting.md) for super-resolution [S1] and triangle mesh approximations for rasterization efficiency [S1].
